assessment: Fresh independent strict review against the unchanged frozen arXiv TeX finds the executable scientific core substantially repaired but not yet source-closed enough for drafting. The corrected AC-KE oracle now exactly materializes g=2*sqrt(max(0,a*((2/3)*x-a))) with a=0.2, and direct execution returns the source-consistent real growth rate at and around threshold: g=0 for x=0,0.29,0.3 and 0.30000000000000004, g=0.4 at x=0.6, and g=0.6110100926607787 at x=1. The standard-WT program returns zero throughout. The private conditions now cleanly identify WT versus AC-KE, while fixed a=0.2, weak nonlinearity, kappa=2/3, and Omega=0 have separate common IDs. However, three requested source-semantic repairs remain incomplete. First, initial_uncorrelated_random_waves still omits the source's homogeneous-statistics qualifier even though that state is the linearization base. Second, the x-domain locator text still falsely says the single experimental ratio at line 420 indicates x in [0,1]; the physical |x|<=1 bound follows instead from the nonnegative power definitions, and [0,1] is an explicit benchmark orientation choice. Third, only the readout statistic and AC applicability localize the 100-realization NLSE confirmation to a=0.2,x=0.6. The AC statement and statistical basis, the WT applicability/statistical basis, and the top-level assessment still broadly say the arbitrary-x claims were validated by NLSE. In the source, AC numerical confirmation is the Fig. 2 setting; WT/NLSE agreement is a different reported thermalization setting; and a direct fiber test of the instability criterion was explicitly precluded. These are remaining card-level locator and scope defects, so no eligible cluster can yet be signed.

issues.detail: The new common-condition structure is almost correct, but initial_uncorrelated_random_waves still says only uncorrelated, zero mean, Gaussian statistics, and m(z=0)=0. Line 325 explicitly states homogeneous statistics for the state about which the AC-KE is linearized. Add that qualifier to the fixed-condition statement and corresponding claim applicability/locator support so both worlds share the exact source-defined initial state. Do not confuse homogeneous statistics in t with the separate homogeneous perturbation mode Omega=0.

The control and both claim domains still use line 420 support text saying the observed relation alpha*L_nl≈0.19>(2/3)DeltaN/N≈0.12 indicates x in [0,1]. That line supplies one positive x≈0.18 case, not the interval. The physical bound |x|<=1 follows algebraically from N=N_x+N_y with nonnegative powers and DeltaN=N_y-N_x (lines 202 and 334). State that the benchmark deliberately chooses the nonnegative orientation 0<=x<=1 from this source-derived bound; retain line 420 only as one observed positive example, not interval support. Apply the same correction to controls, both control_domains, assessment, and source_ambiguity.

The readout statistic and AC applicability now correctly name a=0.2,x=0.6, but the AC claim statement and statistical_basis still say generally that the formula is validated by 100 NLSE realizations. The WT claim applicability/statistical_basis likewise says the a=0.2 arbitrary-x branch is validated by simulations, although the cited WT/NLSE agreement is the distinct Fig. 1 thermalization setup (a=1,x=0). The top-level assessment broadly groups both arbitrary-x claims as NLSE-validated. Revise all these fields consistently: arbitrary-x oracle responses are theoretical closure predictions; the 100-realization AC/NLSE confirmation is only the reported Fig. 2 point a=0.2,x=0.6; WT's zero follows from its defining m=0 closure, with NLSE agreement reported in a different setting; and the fiber experiment did not directly test this instability criterion.

review_material.assessment: The source provides a theoretical prediction for the dimensionless instability growth rate g = Re[lambda(0)] * L_nl as a function of the normalized power difference x = Delta N0/N, with fixed dimensionless coherent coupling a = alpha * L_nl = 0.2. The standard WT closure (m=0) yields g=0, while the AC-KE closure yields g = 2*sqrt(max(0, a*((2/3)*x - a))). The source anchors the definitions of N, Delta N, and the instability criterion. The domain [0,1] is a conservative nonnegative subdomain of |x|<=1, supported by the instability criterion and the experimental parameter values. The claims are theoretical predictions validated by NLSE simulations, not direct fiber measurements. The extraction is complete and case_authoring_ready is true.

review_material.paper_scope: The paper theoretically and experimentally investigates two turbulent regimes in a coherently coupled NLSE system: irreversible thermalization (standard WT) and reversible dynamics mediated by anomalous correlators (AC-KE). The extraction focuses on the theoretical prediction of the dimensionless instability growth rate g = Re[lambda(0)]*L_nl as a function of the normalized power difference x = Delta N0/N, with fixed a = alpha*L_nl = 0.2, comparing the standard WT closure (m=0) and the AC-KE closure.
